meta.title: Who originally recorded "The Best"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Tina Turner. Bonnie Tyler recorded "The Best" first, released January 1988 on CBS. Turner's Capitol version followed in August 1989.
meta.ogDescription: Bonnie Tyler recorded it first, in January 1988 on CBS Records. Tina Turner's 1989 Capitol cover is the version everyone remembers.

answer.label: Not a Tina Turner original — a 1988 Bonnie Tyler single
answer.sourceLine: Almost everyone hears “The Best” as a Tina Turner song, written for her and born with her. It was not. Mike Chapman and Holly Knight wrote it, offered it first to Paul Young — who passed — and Bonnie Tyler made the first recording, issued as the lead single from her album Hide Your Heart in January 1988 on CBS Records. Tyler’s single reached no. 10 in Norway and no. 25 in Finland but spent a single week in the UK chart at no. 95; Turner’s Capitol version arrived in August 1989 and became one of the most recognisable records of her career.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: CBS Records
original.released: Issued as a single on CBS Records in January 1988, ahead of its parent album Hide Your Heart, which followed on 9 May 1988 and carried it as track 7.
original.charted: No. 10 in Norway and no. 25 in Finland, with a no. 8 placing on Italian airplay — but only one week in the UK Singles Chart, at no. 95, and no US chart placing at all.
original.cover: Tina Turner’s version was released on 21 August 1989 on Capitol Records as the lead single from Foreign Affair. It reached no. 5 in the UK and no. 15 on the US Billboard Hot 100, and was certified double platinum in the UK.
trail: Wikipedia’s article on “The Best” ↗ states plainly that Bonnie Tyler recorded the first version, released in January 1988 as the lead single from Hide Your Heart, and that Tina Turner’s version followed on 21 August 1989.
The album entry for Hide Your Heart ↗ confirms the CBS Records issue on 9 May 1988, Desmond Child as producer, and “The Best” at track 7 running 4:16.
The MusicBrainz recording entity ↗ for the Tyler track gives a length of 4:16 on the 1988 Hide Your Heart release — the same runtime as the distributor-supplied audio linked above.

authors.name: Bonnie Tyler
authors.heading: Bonnie Tyler
authors.metaLine: b. 1951, Skewen, Wales · rock and pop singer
authors.bio: Born Gaynor Hopkins in Skewen, Glamorgan in 1951, Tyler built a career on one of the most recognisable voices in British pop — a husky rasp that followed vocal-cord surgery in the 1970s and that carried “It’s a Heartache” and the Jim Steinman–produced “Total Eclipse of the Heart” around the world. Her seventh studio album Hide Your Heart, produced by Desmond Child, carried the first recorded version of “The Best” as its lead single. She has been generous about being eclipsed on it, telling interviewers that Turner did it better than she did — and crediting Turner’s success with restoring her confidence in picking songs. She represented the United Kingdom at Eurovision in 2013 and was appointed MBE in 2022.

authors.name: Tina Turner
authors.heading: Tina Turner
authors.bio: Turner’s version, released in August 1989 as the lead single from Foreign Affair on Capitol Records, is the one the world knows. Before recording it she went to co-writer Holly Knight and asked for two changes: a bridge, which she felt the song was missing, and a key change. Produced by Dan Hartman with Turner and featuring Edgar Winter on saxophone, it reached no. 5 in the UK and no. 15 on the US Billboard Hot 100, went double platinum in Britain, and became so bound up with her name that the two are effectively interchangeable. The only error in the popular memory is chronological — her record really is the definitive one.

authors.name: Mike Chapman & Holly Knight
authors.heading: Mike Chapman & Holly Knight
authors.metaLine: Songwriters · credited on both the 1988 and 1989 recordings
authors.bio: Chapman, the Australian-born producer behind Suzi Quatro, The Sweet and Blondie, wrote “The Best” with the American songwriter Holly Knight, whose catalogue of hard-edged pop anthems runs through Pat Benatar, Heart and Turner herself. The song was pitched to Paul Young first; he turned it down. Knight is also the writer Turner went back to when she wanted the bridge and the key change that reshaped the song into the version now used in stadiums and advertising campaigns.

misattribution.heading: What people get wrong
misattribution.intro: The song is so completely fused with Tina Turner that the existence of an earlier recording surprises most listeners. Here is the record.

items.why: Her Capitol single is the version used in advertising, in sport and in tribute for decades, and it is treated as synonymous with her name.

misattribution.truthLine: Bonnie Tyler recorded it first, in January 1988. Tina Turner recorded it better, in August 1989 — and reshaped it while she was at it.

context.heading: Why the cover swallowed the original
lead: The interesting question is not why Tina Turner had a hit with “The Best” — it is why almost nobody remembers there was anything to cover. Bonnie Tyler’s original was not a flop everywhere; it reached no. 10 in Norway. But in the two markets that write pop history it barely registered, spending exactly one week in the UK chart at no. 95 and never charting in the US at all. A record that faint leaves no memory for a later version to compete with.

Then Turner did something covers rarely do: she changed the architecture. She asked Holly Knight for a bridge and a key change before she would record it, and those additions are precisely the parts the song is now famous for — the lift that makes it work as a stadium record. The Turner version went on to sell Pepsi, Toyotas and T-Mobile contracts, to become the anthem of Australian rugby league after a 1990 campaign, and to attach itself to Ayrton Senna after he appeared during her performance at the 1993 Australian Grand Prix. Decades of that kind of use will overwrite anyone’s memory of a single that lasted seven days at no. 95.
detailsBody: Mike Chapman and Holly Knight write “The Best” and offer it to Paul Young, who declines it.
January 1988 — Bonnie Tyler’s recording is released on CBS Records as the lead single from her forthcoming album.
9 May 1988 — the album Hide Your Heart, produced by Desmond Child, is released; “The Best” is track 7, running 4:16.
The single reaches no. 10 in Norway and no. 25 in Finland, but spends one week in the UK Singles Chart at no. 95 and does not chart in the US.
21 August 1989 — Tina Turner’s version is released on Capitol Records as the lead single from Foreign Affair, with a bridge and key change added at her request.
Turner’s version reaches no. 5 in the UK and no. 15 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and is certified double platinum in the UK.
1992 — Turner re-cuts it as “(Simply) The Best” with Jimmy Barnes to promote the New South Wales Rugby League season, reaching no. 14 in Australia.
context.pull: The original charted for one week in Britain. The cover charted for a generation.
